newsitem.title: UK: Orange branches out into "tree masts".
newsitem.headline: Orange branches out into "tree masts".

text.p: British mobile telephone company Orange Plc on Monday unveils a European first -- a telecommunications mast cunningly disguised as a tree.

In an attempt to quell mounting criticism by environmentalists of the tide of telecom masts spreading across the countryside, Orange has chosen this novel idea for a site on the edge of the picturesque Lake District in northern England.

Orange has nicknamed its experimental mast near Cockermouth "Loquentes per arbores", or talking through trees, and says it has landscaped the area around the transmitter to ensure that there is minimal "visual disruption".
Made of steel tubes coated with an epoxy compound to look like bark and plastic pipe "branches" welded onto a "trunk", the design is based on a conifer -- matching real trees in the area.
The actual aerials are in the "branches", while foliage is made from non-metallic material.
Most masts currently spread across Britain by mobile phone companies are silver lattices of metal, topped by an array of aerials.
Despite protests, more than 8,000 masts have been built with a further 5,000 expected to be built by the end of the decade.

But Orange, partly-owned by Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa Ltd and British Aerospace, has won the approval of local planners for making a conscious effort to protect the beauty of the Lorton valley. ($1=.6167 Pound)
